faq.question: Where exactly is the restaurant?
faq.answer: Bayt Al Ghaf, Unit 14, Heritage Quarter, Al Seef Street, Al Seef, Bur Dubai, Dubai, United Arab Emirates. We are on the Al Seef creek-side promenade in Bur Dubai, about 400 m (5 minutes' walk) from the Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood. The entrance is Heritage Quarter Gate 3 on Al Seef Street. (Fictional test address.)

faq.question: What is the easiest way to get there from a nearby landmark?
faq.answer: From the Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, walk towards the creek and turn left along the Al Seef promenade — about 5 minutes. From Al Fahidi Metro Station (Green Line) it is a 10-minute walk towards the creek. From Deira, take an abra to Bur Dubai Abra Station and walk 12 minutes along the creek.

faq.question: Is parking available?
faq.answer: Yes, paid public parking along Al Seef Street and in the Al Seef multi-storey car park (about 3 minutes' walk), paid through the official parking app, SMS or machines. Valet parking runs at Gate 3 from 18:00 to 24:00 on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays (AED 40, paid to the operator). There are two accessible bays beside Gate 3 and a 10-minute drop-off bay for takeaway. The restaurant cannot reserve parking.

faq.question: Can I get there by metro or public transport?
faq.answer: Yes. Take the Green Line to Al Fahidi Metro Station and walk about 10 minutes towards the creek. Buses stop at Al Ghubaiba Bus Station and on Al Fahidi Street (10–12 minutes' walk). From Deira you can cross the creek by abra.

faq.question: What should I tell my taxi driver?
faq.answer: “Al Seef, Heritage Quarter, Gate 3, near Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, Bur Dubai.” Ride-hailing drop-off is at the Gate 3 lay-by on Al Seef Street.

faq.question: How far is it from the airport?
faq.answer: About 15–25 minutes by taxi from Dubai International Airport (DXB), depending on traffic.

faq.question: What time do you open and close?
faq.answer: Monday to Thursday and Sunday 08:00–23:00; Friday and Saturday 08:00–midnight. The kitchen takes last orders 30 minutes before closing. Breakfast is served 08:00–11:30. Hours change during Ramadan and on some holidays — check the date.

faq.question: When is breakfast served?
faq.answer: Daily 08:00–11:30 (not during Ramadan). The Weekend Fuala Breakfast Spread is served on Saturdays and Sundays from 08:00 to 12:00.

faq.question: What time is the last order?
faq.answer: 30 minutes before closing: 22:30 Monday–Thursday and Sunday, 23:30 on Friday and Saturday. The last table reservation starts 90 minutes before closing.

faq.question: Can you stay open two hours after closing for my group?
faq.answer: No. We cannot extend opening hours for individual guests or groups. For a late private event, the events team can discuss a private booking in advance, but nothing beyond the published hours can be promised by phone.

faq.question: Are you open on public holidays?
faq.answer: Yes, normally with regular hours. Exceptions (for example the first day of Eid Al Fitr, when we open at 14:00) are listed in the special-days calendar and returned by the hours API for that date.

faq.question: Can I reserve a table for six people tomorrow evening?
faq.answer: Usually yes — tables for 6 are booked for 120 minutes, and we take bookings up to 90 minutes before closing. Availability depends on the exact time, so we check live availability for the date, time and seating area and then book with your name and phone number.

faq.question: How far in advance can I book?
faq.answer: Up to 60 days ahead, and at least 30 minutes before the time. Majlis rooms need 24 hours' notice.

faq.question: What is the largest group you can book?
faq.answer: 20 guests. Groups of 13–20 are held as a request and confirmed by the team. For more than 20 guests or a private event, contact events@baytalghaf.example.

faq.question: Can I request an outdoor table or a particular seating area?
faq.answer: Yes — indoor, window (creek view), terrace (outdoor, mid-October to end of April, weather permitting) or a private majlis room (6+ guests). If the requested area is full we will tell you and offer another time or area; we never move you without asking. We cannot promise a specific table number.

faq.question: Can you promise me a window table?
faq.answer: Only if a window table is free and booked for you — the confirmation then says “creek-view window tables”. If every window table is booked we cannot make one available; we can offer another time with a window table or a different area.

faq.question: Can I change or cancel my reservation?
faq.answer: Yes. Changes can be made until 2 hours before the booking (subject to availability). Cancellation is free any time before the booking. You will need the booking reference and the phone number used to book.

faq.question: What happens if I am late for my reservation?
faq.answer: We hold the table for 15 minutes. After that it may be given to other guests. Please call if you are running late.

faq.question: Do you take walk-ins?
faq.answer: Yes. Some tables are kept for walk-in guests every day, subject to availability. Friday and Saturday evenings are busy, so booking is recommended.

faq.question: Can I reserve a table without giving a phone number?
faq.answer: No. A phone number is required for every reservation so we can confirm or contact you about the booking. International numbers are fine with their country code.

faq.question: Is there a deposit or cancellation fee?
faq.answer: No deposit or card guarantee for regular tables. Majlis rooms have a minimum spend of AED 150 per person, settled after the meal.

faq.question: What is the majlis room?
faq.answer: A private room with traditional floor seating (cushions and low tables). Majlis Al Sidr seats 6–10 (low chairs on request) and Majlis Al Ghaf seats 10–20. Book at least 24 hours ahead; minimum spend AED 150 per person; bookings last 180 minutes.

faq.question: Can I order food now and collect it when I arrive?
faq.answer: Yes. Place a pickup order for a time at least the kitchen lead time away (minimum 20 minutes, longer for dishes like grilled fish). We confirm the exact ready time; collect at the takeaway counter at Gate 3 with your order number. If you are dining in, book a table and add a dine-in pre-order so food is ready when you sit down.

faq.question: How early should I place a takeaway order?
faq.answer: At least 20 minutes ahead, or the longest dish's preparation time plus 10 minutes (e.g. 30 minutes if you order Hammour Mashwi). Busy slots can fill up — the system offers the nearest free time. You can order up to 7 days ahead.

faq.question: Can I order without making a reservation?
faq.answer: Yes. Pickup and delivery orders do not need a reservation. Only a dine-in pre-order (food ready at your table) needs a confirmed reservation.

faq.question: Can I place an order over the phone?
faq.answer: Yes. Our phone assistant can take pickup and delivery orders and dine-in pre-orders using the same system as the website, and will read back the confirmed details and order number.

faq.question: Can I order for someone else?
faq.answer: Yes. Give your own name and phone number as the customer and add the name (and phone, if different) of the person collecting or receiving the order. They should quote the order number at the counter.

faq.question: What happens if I arrive late for pickup?
faq.answer: Orders are held for 60 minutes after the pickup time. Food is best within about 30 minutes. After 60 minutes the order may be marked “not collected” and is not kept for food-safety reasons. If you will be late, call — if cooking has not started we can move the time.

faq.question: Can I change my order after it is confirmed?
faq.answer: Yes, until 30 minutes before the pickup or delivery time, or until the kitchen starts preparing it (whichever is earlier). Changes are re-checked for availability and price. Changing a regular order into a large one (more than 20 portions) needs a catering order with advance notice.

faq.question: Can I cancel my order?
faq.answer: Yes, free of charge until the kitchen starts preparing it. After that, please call the restaurant. No payment is taken in advance for regular orders.

faq.question: How long does a particular dish take to prepare?
faq.answer: Each dish has a preparation time in the menu (for example Lamb Machboos 15 minutes, Hammour Mashwi 20 minutes, Luqaimat 10 minutes, Karak 5 minutes). The order lead time is the longest dish plus a short buffer.

faq.question: How do I check the status of my order?
faq.answer: Use the order number and the phone number used to order, on the website's Track Order page or by phone. Statuses: received, confirmed, being prepared, ready, completed.

faq.question: Do you deliver?
faq.answer: Yes, within central Dubai, 12:00–22:30, with our own drivers. Fees start at AED 7 (minimum order AED 50) for nearby areas. Breakfast is not delivered and some dishes are pickup-only.

faq.question: Can you deliver to Abu Dhabi in 15 minutes?
faq.answer: No. We deliver only within Dubai, and no delivery can arrive faster than the kitchen lead time plus the drive time. Pickup from Al Seef is always available.

faq.question: Which areas do you deliver to?
faq.answer: Zone A — Old Dubai (AED 7, min AED 50): Al Seef, Al Fahidi, Bur Dubai, Al Souq Al Kabeer, Al Hamriya, Mankhool, Al Raffa, Umm Hurair 1, Al Ghubaiba. Zone B — Creek & Deira (AED 12, min AED 80): Al Karama, Oud Metha, Umm Hurair 2, Al Jaddaf, Za'abeel, Al Satwa, Al Bada'a, Deira, Al Ras, Al Rigga, Port Saeed, Al Muraqqabat, Al Sabkha. Zone C — Downtown & Garhoud (AED 18, min AED 120): Downtown Dubai, Business Bay, DIFC, Trade Centre, Jumeirah 1, Al Wasl, Al Garhoud, Dubai Festival City, Ras Al Khor, Dubai Healthcare City. Further areas such as Dubai Marina and Palm Jumeirah are covered for catering orders only.

faq.question: Can I order 40 meals for an office?
faq.answer: Yes, as a catering order with at least 24 hours' notice — for example 40 Office Machboos Lunch Boxes at AED 45 each. We give a quote first; the catering team then confirms within 4 hours.

faq.question: Can I order 100 portions for an event?
faq.answer: Yes, with at least 48 hours' notice and if catering capacity is available that day (300 portions per day in total). Orders of 51–100 portions get 5% off food. A 50% deposit applies above AED 2,500. The order is pending until the catering team confirms.

faq.question: What is the most you can cater?
faq.answer: 250 portions per order and 300 portions per day across all catering orders. Larger events go to the events team (events@baytalghaf.example).

faq.question: What is included in a family platter?
faq.answer: Majlis Sharing Platter (AED 329, serves 4, daily): lamb machboos with hashu, two portions of chicken saloona, eight sambousa, a large house salad, dakkus and twenty luqaimat. Friday Family Machboos Platter (AED 349, serves 5, Fridays only): lamb shoulder and a whole chicken on machboos rice with hashu, dakkus, large salad, five laban and twenty luqaimat.

faq.question: Do you do a whole lamb (ouzi)?
faq.answer: Yes — Whole Lamb Ouzi (AED 1,450) serves 10–12, catering only, with at least 48 hours' notice and a maximum of 3 per day.

faq.question: What is machboos?
faq.answer: The Emirati national rice dish: meat (lamb, chicken or camel) or vegetables cooked with basmati rice in stock spiced with bezar and dried black lime (loomi), topped with hashu (caramelised onions and raisins).

faq.question: What ingredients are in a particular dish?
faq.answer: Every dish has a full ingredient list with quantities in the menu catalogue and the API (`GET /api/v1/menu/items/{id}`), including each sauce's own ingredients.

faq.question: What exactly is in each sauce?
faq.answer: Every sauce, marinade, spice blend and topping is documented with full composition per batch, allergens, spice level and the dishes it is used in. Our house preparations are Al Ghaf House Red, Al Ghaf House Green, Sauce No. 7 and the Bezar spice blend.

faq.question: What is in Sauce No. 7?
faq.answer: Tamarind, date syrup, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, garlic, ginger, ground loomi, sugar and our bezar spice blend. It contains soy, wheat (gluten, from the soy sauce) and sesame. It glazes the lamb chops and the camel burger.

faq.question: Can the chef make a dish less spicy?
faq.answer: For most stews and grills, yes — choose a milder spice level or “no chilli”. Machboos is already mild and cannot be made milder because the rice cooks in spiced stock; its heat comes from the dakkus served on the side, which you can skip. Each dish's spice options are listed in the menu.

faq.question: Can an ingredient be removed?
faq.answer: Many can — e.g. raisins from the hashu, pine nuts from the hummus, croutons from the lentil soup, sesame seeds from luqaimat, cheese from the burger. Only the listed options are possible; ingredients cooked into a base (stock, batter, marinade) cannot be removed. Removing an ingredient does not remove traces.

faq.question: Do you serve camel?
faq.answer: Yes: Camel Kofta (AED 76) and the Camel Burger (AED 72) every day, Camel Machboos (AED 92) on Thursdays, and Date & Camel Milk Ice Cream. All camel meat is halal.

faq.question: Do you serve alcohol or shisha?
faq.answer: No. Bayt Al Ghaf is alcohol-free and does not offer shisha or allow smoking.

faq.question: Is the food halal?
faq.answer: Yes. All meat and poultry are halal and no pork or pork products are used.

faq.question: Which dish has rice, meat and dried lemon?
faq.answer: That sounds like machboos — most likely Lamb Machboos (AED 72): lamb and basmati rice cooked with loomi (dried black lime) and bezar. Chicken Machboos and Thursday's Camel Machboos are similar.

faq.question: Does this dish contain nuts, dairy, gluten, sesame or shellfish?
faq.answer: Each dish lists the allergens it contains as ingredients and the ones it may contain as traces (menu catalogue, allergen matrix and the API). Ask about a specific dish and we will read its list. We cannot guarantee any dish is free of an allergen.

faq.question: Can you guarantee there is absolutely no cross-contamination?
faq.answer: Our single kitchen handles cereals containing gluten (wheat), crustaceans (prawns/shrimp), eggs, fish, soy, milk / dairy, tree nuts, celery, mustard, sesame, sulphites. We do not use molluscs, peanuts, lupin as ingredients, but supplier products may carry traces. We take care to limit cross-contact, but we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from any allergen. Guests with severe allergies should speak to the duty manager before ordering.

faq.question: Can you make the entire menu nut-free?
faq.answer: No. Several dishes use tree nuts (walnuts in Al Ghaf House Red, pine nuts on the hummus and ouzi, pistachio crumb, almonds) and they are handled in our single kitchen. We can show dishes with no nut ingredients and leave nut garnishes off where an option exists, but we cannot offer a nut-free kitchen.

faq.question: I am allergic to sesame. Is your house sauce safe?
faq.answer: Which house sauce do you mean? Al Ghaf House Red and Al Ghaf House Green have no sesame ingredients, but Sauce No. 7 contains sesame oil, and sesame is used in our kitchen, so we cannot say any sauce is definitely safe. Please speak to the duty manager for a severe allergy.

faq.question: Which dishes are vegetarian or vegan?
faq.answer: Vegan (as served): Shorbat Adas, Nakhi, Salatat Al Bait (House Salad), Vegetable Machboos, Bamia Saloona, Pumpkin & Chickpea Saloona, Gahwa Emirati (Dallah for the Table), Sulaimani, Limon Na'na. Vegetarian with dairy or egg: Balaleet, Chebab with Date Syrup & Cream Cheese, Regag with Egg & Cheese, Bayd w Tamat, Weekend Fuala Breakfast Spread, Luqaimat, Khanfaroosh, Date & Camel Milk Ice Cream, Aseedat Bobar (Winter Pumpkin Asida), Karak Chai, Chilled Laban with Mint, Date & Cardamom Shake. The full lists, including dishes that can be made vegetarian with an option, are in the dietary guide.

faq.question: Do you have a vegan seafood platter?
faq.answer: No. We do not make plant-based seafood. Vegan options are our vegetable machboos and saloona dishes and several starters.

faq.question: Is the lamb machboos dairy-free?
faq.answer: No. It contains Milk / dairy, Sulphites — the rice is finished with ghee and the hashu is cooked in ghee.

faq.question: Is anything gluten-free?
faq.answer: Several dishes have no gluten-containing ingredients (for example the saloona dishes with rice, machboos, grilled fish, salad), but nothing is certified gluten-free: wheat is used throughout the kitchen and fryers are shared. Guests with coeliac disease should speak to the duty manager.

faq.question: Which items are available on Fridays?
faq.answer: Everything on the permanent menu plus the Friday Family Machboos Platter (AED 349, serves 5, 12:00–22:00, pickup or dine-in, order 2 hours ahead). Weekday specials from other days (Monday fish saloona, Tuesday margooga, Wednesday madrooba, Thursday camel machboos) are not served on Friday.

faq.question: Is the Ramadan menu available outside Ramadan?
faq.answer: No. The Iftar Set Menu is served only during Ramadan (provisionally Monday 8 February 2027 to Tuesday 9 March 2027). Many of its dishes are on the regular menu all year.

faq.question: What are your Ramadan hours?
faq.answer: During Ramadan we open 12:00–24:00. Breakfast is not served; iftar seating starts at 17:30 and the Iftar Set Menu (minimum 2) must be ordered by 14:00 for the same day.

faq.question: Do you have a UAE National Day special?
faq.answer: Yes — the Eid Al Etihad Feast (AED 355, serves 4) on 1–3 December 2026. Pre-orders open on 15 November 2026, at least 24 hours ahead.

faq.question: Can I order your Friday platter for Tuesday?
faq.answer: No — it is only cooked on Fridays, at any price. You can pre-order it on any day for collection on a Friday, or order the Majlis Sharing Platter (serves 4) on Tuesday.

faq.question: Is there a seasonal dessert?
faq.answer: Aseedat Bobar, a warm winter pumpkin asida with ghee, saffron and cardamom, is served from 1 November 2026 to 28 February 2027.

faq.question: What payment methods are accepted?
faq.answer: Cash (AED only); Visa, Mastercard and American Express (chip & PIN or contactless); Apple Pay and Google Pay (contactless at the counter or table). Online orders are paid on collection, on delivery or at the table — there is no online card payment and we never take card numbers by phone.

faq.question: Do prices include VAT? Is there a service charge?
faq.answer: Yes, all prices include 5% VAT. There is no service charge; tipping is optional. Delivery fees are shown separately.

faq.question: What is the cheapest way to feed 15 people?
faq.answer: It depends on the day and the dishes available. We calculate it from live prices with the feeding-suggestions tool (main dishes only), e.g. a mix of machboos portions and sharing platters. Orders above 20 kitchen portions become catering orders with advance notice.

faq.question: Can you accommodate children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children are welcome; we have 6 high chairs (request up to 4 with a booking) and a baby-changing table. There is no separate children's menu; the team can advise smaller portions on the day.

faq.question: Is the restaurant wheelchair accessible?
faq.answer: Yes: step-free entrance from Gate 3 and the promenade, an accessible restroom, accessible tables in the main hall, by the window and on the terrace (via a ramp), and two accessible parking bays at Gate 3. The majlis rooms use floor seating.

faq.question: Can I bring my own birthday cake?
faq.answer: Yes, with notice in the reservation's special requests; a plating fee of AED 30 applies. Other outside food and drink is not permitted.

faq.question: Are pets allowed?
faq.answer: Pets are not allowed inside or on the terrace. Assistance dogs are welcome.

faq.question: What happens if an item becomes unavailable after I order?
faq.answer: The team removes it from the order, re-totals it and calls you to offer a substitute of similar value or to cancel. You are never charged for an item you do not receive.

faq.question: How can I report a missing or incorrect item?
faq.answer: Within 24 hours, call or WhatsApp +971 50 555 0142 with your order number and, if possible, a photo. We will replace the item or refund/credit it. Refunds for items paid by card go back to the original card through the restaurant's card terminal; cash payments are refunded in cash or as a credit note. No card details are ever taken over the phone.

faq.question: How do refunds work?
faq.answer: As payment is taken in person, most cancellations involve no refund at all. When a refund is due: Refunds for items paid by card go back to the original card through the restaurant's card terminal; cash payments are refunded in cash or as a credit note. No card details are ever taken over the phone.

faq.question: What does Bayt Al Ghaf mean?
faq.answer: “House of the Ghaf” — the ghaf (Prosopis cineraria) is the UAE's national tree, a symbol of shade, endurance and hospitality in the desert.

faq.question: Is this a real restaurant?
faq.answer: Bayt Al Ghaf is a fictional restaurant created as a realistic test environment. Its address, phone numbers, e-mail addresses, availability, prices and policies are simulated. Do not travel to, call, or pay this business.
